name: Population budget and market access
technology: c.200 AD food model; walking access without roads or ships

sources.title: Klein Goldewijk et al. 2017, HYDE 3.2, section 3.1
sources.use: Population totals and spatial allocation are separate; historical allocation uses environmental proxies. No HYDE Earth raster or population count is transplanted into this world.

sources.title: Tobler 1993, NCGIA Technical Report 93-1
sources.use: Signed slope walking speed: 6 exp(-3.5 abs(s + 0.05)) km/h; 0.6 off-path factor. Slope is rise/run, not degrees.

assumptions: The population total is supplied by the user; the initial value is the existing central occupation scenario for this climate. This model reallocates a census, rather than predicting its total.
Environmental support is the existing Harvest settlement potential in people/km2, with optional removal of its malaria penalty. It is a local support ceiling for this experiment.
Attraction weights are explicit scenario choices, inspired by HYDE's use of environmental proxies; they are not HYDE coefficients or independent validation.
All named places are potential markets, with no assumed city population. Nearest market travel follows an eight-neighbour directed land graph. Water and blocked diagonal corners cannot be crossed.
Walking hours exclude rest, roads, boats, bridges, border costs and seasonal closures. Island land without a reachable named market retains a positive settlement weight.

Allocated people never exceed local environmental support. Excess requested population is reported separately, never silently dropped. Imports and urban densities above local food support are not simulated.
Market catchment totals describe surrounding residents, not city population. Population pressure and spare support use the same capacity and allocated population, so their food budget is consistent.
